llm.summary: This is a disclosed dLazy image-generation wrapper that uses a pinned CLI, sends prompts and chosen media files to dLazy, and stores a dLazy API key locally.

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses that prompts and parameters go to api.dlazy.com and user-supplied media paths are uploaded to files.dlazy.com, which is proportionate for a hosted image-generation service.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses the external npm package @dlazy/cli pinned to version 1.2.3, with an npx alternative and source/provenance links disclosed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger phrases are broad and the error-handling text uses strong agent-directed wording, but the instructions stay within invoking the image tool and explaining authentication or balance errors.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The CLI stores a dLazy API key in ~/.dlazy/config.json or the Windows user profile equivalent; this is disclosed, scoped to the dLazy service, and revocable, with no system persistence or privilege escalation shown.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented capability, CLI command, API endpoints, authentication flow, and image-generation purpose are coherent and purpose-aligned.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, confirm you intend to use dLazy's hosted service for image generation. Prompts and selected media files may be sent to dLazy, generated outputs are hosted by dLazy, and authentication may save an API key locally. Prefer npx for non-global use and review the external CLI package if supply-chain risk matters to you.
llm.findings:
[AE1] unexpected: The linked English and Chinese markdown files are present in the artifact and were inspected, so the partial-inspection concern is not supported by the local package.
[SQP-1] expected: The generic image trigger terms are broad, but they match the skill's stated image generation/editing purpose; users should still be aware this may route image requests to dLazy.
[P9] unexpected: The whitespace finding corresponds to wide markdown table formatting; manual inspection found no hidden instructions after the padding.
[SQP-3] expected: The agent-directed error guidance is commercially oriented and strongly worded, but it is limited to telling users about insufficient credits or missing API keys for the same service.
[AIG-SARIF] expected: The supplied static scan reported no T01-T09 security findings.
